topic: Newton's Second Law: Force, Mass, and Acceleration
key_concepts: Acceleration is a change in speed and/or direction over time
Acceleration results from an unbalanced net force
Balanced forces produce zero net force and no acceleration
Net force and acceleration act in the same direction
Acceleration is directly proportional to net force at constant mass
Acceleration is inversely proportional to mass under constant force
The relationship among net force, mass, and acceleration is expressed as a = F/m
Greater applied force produces greater acceleration for a given mass
Greater mass produces smaller acceleration for the same force
Graphs of acceleration versus force are straight lines, while acceleration versus mass gra
Gravitational force on a hanging mass can be an applied force and equals mg
Acceleration due to gravity is 9.8 m/s^2
